newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X halted after mine permits canceled.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X halted after mine permits canceled.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq on Wednesday after the Indonesian government said it canceled parliamentary approval for mining permits essential to Bre-X's future.
"We cancel it. The Bre-X contract of work will be processed from the beginning," Indonesian Mine Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said today in Jakarta.
He said his ministry was investigating whether Bre-X misrepresented its status about the massive Busang gold find in Indonesia to U.S. regulatory authorities.
Umar Said, the secretary-general of mines, said the government was also checking with Indonesian capital markets surveillance officials "to see if this is criminal."
"I would perceive this as negative (for Bre-X) only because they used the word 'criminal,'" said gold analyst Catherine Gignac with Deacon Capital in Toronto.
She said Bre-X needed to explain to shareholders what the move meant for its rights to Busang.
"Does Bre-X lose everything? We have no idea," she said.

Bre-X was in the midst of negotiations with Toronto's Barrick Gold Corp over Busang. The Indonesian government had asked the companies to form a joint venture for the property, with Barrick getting 75 percent and Bre-X keeping 25 percent.
The two companies did not finalize an agreement before a December 4 deadline set by the Indonesian government, but the consequences of that have been unclear.
The Indonesian government has been under international pressure to open up the bidding process for the gold property, analyst Gignac said.
Barrick did not return calls to say whether it was still interested in negotiating with Bre-X.
